question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject unsafe byte-size config values instead of preserving the previous rounded behavior for existing configs?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but root policy treats stricter config validation as compatibility-sensitive because existing user config can fail or change behavior after upgrade.

options.title: Accept safe-integer cutoff
options.body: Land this PR as the canonical behavior because JavaScript cannot represent those byte values exactly and silent rounding is worse than validation failure.

options.title: Preserve upgrade compatibility
options.body: Ask for a warning, doctor guidance, or compatibility path if maintainers want existing unsafe values to keep loading during upgrade.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the PR open until a config owner decides whether this stricter validation belongs in this release train.

recommendation.title: Accept safe-integer cutoff
recommendation.body: Land this PR as the canonical behavior because JavaScript cannot represent those byte values exactly and silent rounding is worse than validation failure.
